title: Super Easy Sourdough Cookbook for Beginners: Simple Step-by-Step Recipes for Artisan Bread
description: Tired of watching sourdough tutorials online only to end up with dense, gummy loaves that never rise? Frustrated by confusing instructions that assume you already know how sourdough starters, hydration, and fermentation work? You're not alone. Super Easy Sourdough Cookbook for Beginners takes the guesswork out of homemade sourdough baking with clear, step-by-step guidance, beginner-friendly recipes, and everyday ingredients. Whether you're creating your first sourdough starter or baking artisan bread for your family, this practical guide helps you build confidence one loaf at a time—no fancy bakery equipment or professional experience required. title: Sourdough: A Novel
description: From Robin Sloan, the New York Times bestselling author of Mr. Penumbra’s 24-Hour Bookstore , comes Sourdough , "a perfect parable for our times" ( San Francisco Magazine ): a delicious and funny novel about an overworked and under-socialized software engineer discovering a calling and a community as a baker. Named One of the Best Books of the Year by NPR, the San Francisco Chronicle , and Southern Living Lois Clary is a software engineer at General Dexterity, a San Francisco robotics company with world-changing ambitions. She codes all day and collapses at night, her human contact limited to the two brothers who run the neighborhood hole-in-the-wall from which she orders dinner every evening. Then, disaster! Visa issues. The brothers quickly close up shop. But they have one last delivery for Lois: their culture, the sourdough starter used to bake their bread. She must keep it alive, they tell her—feed it daily, play it music, and learn to bake with it. Lois is no baker, but she could use a roommate, even if it is a needy colony of microorganisms. Soon, not only is she eating her own homemade bread, she’s providing loaves to the General Dexterity cafeteria every day. title: Sourdough Troubleshooting for Beginners: Fix Dense Bread, Gummy Crumb, Flat Loaves & Weak
description: YOUR SOURDOUGH LOOKS NOTHING LIKE THE LOAF YOU HOPED FOR? You followed the recipe. You fed your starter, waited for the dough to rise, shaped your loaf, and baked it with anticipation. But the result was dense, gummy, flat, or disappointing. The problem may not be your recipe. It may be your starter, fermentation, dough temperature, flour, shaping, or baking technique. Sourdough Troubleshooting for Beginners helps you understand what went wrong, recognise the clues, and make targeted corrections instead of guessing at every bake. STOP GUESSING. START UNDERSTANDING YOUR DOUGH. Sourdough baking becomes less frustrating when you know what to look for. Instead of changing several ingredients or techniques at once, learn how to use the evidence your starter, dough, crumb, and crust provide. Inside this practical guide, you'll discover how to: Revive a weak sourdough starter and recognise the difference between slow activity, hunger, and possible contamination. Troubleshoot dense bread and tight crumb by investigating fermentation, gluten development, flour, hydration, and shaping. Fix gummy or wet bread inside by examining baking time, cooling, fermentation, and moisture. Understand flat loaves and poor oven spring and distinguish likely fermentation problems from weaknesses in dough structure. Recognise overproofing and underproofing instead of relying blindly on recipe timings. Handle sticky, slack dough and improve your approach to shaping and dough strength. Improve crust, flavour, scoring, and crumb structure with practical observations and targeted adjustments. A PRACTICAL REFERENCE FOR YOUR NEXT BAKE This is more than a list of common sourdough mistakes. It gives you a repeatable way to investigate problems and learn from each loaf.
